scope: Responsive desktop and phone web apps; open-source-first; Dodo Payments billing

recommendation.backend: Supabase Auth, PostgreSQL, Storage; MIT JavaScript and SSR clients
recommendation.ui: Existing MakerKit/shadcn UI foundation, Tailwind, forms, tables, and Recharts

billing.reason_for_sdk_over_framework_adapter: The SDK has an explicit Apache-2.0 license. The dodo-adapters repository has a GPL-3.0 root license, and its published Next.js and Better Auth package metadata omits a license. Prefer the explicitly permissive SDK for our reusable base.

rationale: Provides authentication, password reset, email verification, MFA, profile settings, account deletion, and an account schema rather than a minimal login demo.
Account and avatar storage policies in the SQL migration scope access to auth.uid(). These are useful reference policies, not a substitute for testing each new application table.
Keeps authentication and storage in the same managed backend; ordinary PostgreSQL and Next.js are broadly reusable.
Root source is MIT and billing can use Dodo's Apache-2.0 SDK.
Avoids replacing a large Stripe-centric billing model or introducing the Wasp framework and its Windows WSL requirement.
required_before_production: Upgrade Next.js and @next/bundle-analyzer from 16.3.0; regenerate the lockfile and verify compatibility. Next.js 16.3.8 was the current stable release and returned no matching advisories in the scoped OSV query on the evaluation date.

Remove the unused @makerkit/data-loader-supabase-core and @makerkit/data-loader-supabase-nextjs dependencies and catalog entries. Their npm artifacts have no license notice; their linked source monorepo has an AGPL-3.0 root license. No source imports were found in the Lite snapshot.
Implement and test the reusable Dodo checkout, authenticated customer portal, subscription/entitlement sync, and durable duplicate-event handling.
Enable E2E CI and mobile Chrome/Mobile Safari projects. They are optional or commented out in the audited source.
Configure Supabase, OAuth/email delivery, Dodo test products and signed webhooks, deployment, secrets, backups, and runtime monitoring.
Run build, lint, type checks, account and access-isolation tests, Dodo sandbox flows, and desktop/phone usability checks.
